text:
Lina (Design): Dropped an alternate compact layout for the Alerting "preview sidebar" — goal is denser signal for teams with many channels. Two variants: stacked cards (current) vs condensed table (new). Screenshot + Figma link: https://figma.redwood/alert-preview-compact

Omar (PM): Condensed table seems promising for power users. Concern: does it still surface suppression reasons clearly? Hard to scan long lists if reasons wrap.

Jules (Frontend): Table is doable. Proposal: keep a single-line reason column with truncation and a tooltip for full reason. Use `title` attribute + accessible tooltip component. Also make the left-most column a reorder handle for drag-drop reorder.

Priya (Eng-Accessibility): Table semantics are fine if we use proper <table> structure; however keyboard focus jumps between cells can be confusing. Recommend `role=\"list\"` with each row as `role=\"listitem\"` and provide `aria-describedby` pointing to reason. Also tooltips need accessible dismiss/escape.

Mason (SRE): Important: when a suppression rule is time-windowed (quiet hours), we should show the active window inline, e.g., "Quiet 22:00-07:00 (local)". For teams operating across timezones, show both policy timezone and user's timezone in hint.

Lina (Design): Ok — show local time + policy time in smaller text under reason. Also thinking about color: red states for "failed" and amber for "rate-limited". Priya flagged contrast on amber in dark mode previously.

Omar (PM): Copy nits: change "suppressed" to "silenced" in the compact view? It's shorter but may be less clear. What do folks prefer?

Jules (Frontend): "Silenced" is concise. We should keep a hover tooltip that expands to "silenced by quiet window" to preserve clarity.

Priya (Eng-Accessibility): Word choice matters for screen readers too. "Silenced" vs "suppressed" both ok; but include a phrase in the accessible label that mentions the reason: `aria-label=\"Channel PagerDuty — silenced by quiet window until 07:00\"`. That gives SRs full context without forcing visible copy to be long.

Mason (SRE): Another improvement: show a small indicator when a channel has an active escalation policy attached (pager duty). That way ops knows reroutes might happen. Maybe a badge: "escalation" or small arrow icon linking to policy.

Lina (Design): Will add an escalation icon column. For the condensed table, I want to include an inline toggle to expand the channel into a mini-log (last match, last sent, last suppressed). Expand should be keyboard accessible and maintain focus order.

Jules (Frontend): Implementation note: use an ARIA disclosure pattern. Each row is a <button aria-expanded=\"false\"> that toggles a sibling <div role=\"region\" aria-hidden=\"true\">. Also for performance, we should virtualize the list for accounts with 100s of channels.

Priya (Eng-Accessibility): When virtualizing, ensure offscreen rows are not focusable and not announced. Use `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize` for accurate position announcements when navigating with screen readers.

Omar (PM): UX question: should simulation (preview) respect the user's channel order or show sorted by relevance? Maybe default to user order but add a column header control to sort by state (notified/ silenced / fallback).

Lina (Design): I'll wire a small toolbar: [Order: User v. Auto] + [Filter: All | Notified | Silenced | Failed] + compact/dense toggle. Defaults: User order + All + Dense off.

Mason (SRE): On filtering: make sure the filter state is included in the shareable preview URL so folks can link to a filtered view in runbooks. Example: `?filter=silenced&order=user`.

Jules (Frontend): Will add query params and keep the API stateless. Also, small aria note: the filter buttons should have `aria-pressed` and be grouped in a `role=\"toolbar\"`.

Priya (Eng-Accessibility): Contrast again: the table row separators in dark mode are almost invisible. Increase divider opacity and ensure focus ring is visible. Also, when a row is expanded, announce "Row expanded: last matched 2m ago" using `aria-live` polite so SR users receive immediate feedback.

deploy-bot: preview build succeeded — url: https://preview.redwood/alerts/preview-compact?branch=compact-view

Lina (Design): Thanks — I'll iterate on the truncated reason tooltip copy and add the timezone hint. Planning to ship opt-in as `compact preview` in the next feature flag release. Please reply with any must-have accessibility or SRE data points before EOD.

Omar (PM): Add to the TODO: ensure the shareable URL masks PII in policy names.

Jules (Frontend): Noted. I'll mask names client-side before putting them in the querystring, and we'll store anonymized IDs server-side.

Priya (Eng-Accessibility): Quick checklist I'll send: aria-live summary, keyboard disclosure, focus management with virtualization, contrast tokens updated, tooltip accessible.

Mason (SRE): I'll draft a short section for runbooks on how to interpret the compact preview and what variants mean (user order vs algorithmic).

Lina (Design): Great teamwork. Small thumbs up if no further blockers. :thumbsup:
